title: Noch viel Luft nach oben
text:
Die App Couple Joy hat ein paar nette Ansätze, allerdings gibt es einige erhebliche Schwächen, die den Nutzungsspaß deutlich mindern. Der größte Kritikpunkt: Die App ist komplett auf heteronormative Paare ausgelegt. Gleichgeschlechtliche Paare oder Konstellationen zwischen anderen Geschlechtern und Identitäten werden hier kaum berücksichtigt. Es wird stark mit heteronormativen Klischees gearbeitet, was nicht nur einschränkend, sondern auch unangemessen ist.

Ein weiteres großes Manko ist das Fehlen einer automatischen Übersetzungsfunktion für die Antworten. In einer Beziehung, in der Partner:innen unterschiedliche Muttersprachen sprechen, kann dies zu erheblichen Verständnisschwierigkeiten führen. Man muss sich auf eine gemeinsame Sprache einigen, was den Spaß und die Leichtigkeit der Nutzung erheblich mindert.

Auch die Fragenlogik der App lässt zu wünschen übrig. Paare, die erst wenige Wochen zusammen sind, werden nach gemeinsamen Urlauben gefragt und sollen dazu Fotos hochladen. Das ist für frische Beziehungen nicht nur verwirrend, sondern auch frustrierend. Statt das Kennenlernen zu fördern, führt es zu unnötigem Druck und Missverständnissen.

Zusätzlich sind die Fragen im Spiel „Niemals habe ich“ teilweise missverständlich formuliert. Man ist sich oft unsicher, welchen der beiden Buttons man wählen soll, was den Spielspaß erheblich reduziert.

Die App hat grundsätzlich Potenzial, ist aber momentan stark verbesserungswürdig. Insbesondere die Einschränkung auf heteronormative Paare und das Fehlen einer automatischen Übersetzung machen sie für viele Paare uninteressant. In ihrem aktuellen Zustand kann ich sie nicht weiterempfehlen und werde mein Jahresabo nicht verlängern. Wenn diese grundlegenden Probleme angegangen werden, könnte die App deutlich attraktiver werden.

title: Tolle Idee - aber fehlerhaft
text:
Ich habe die App runtergeladen und direkt ein Quiz gemacht, das sehr gut auf meinen Freund und mich anwendbar war, daher hat danach mein Freund die Fragen auf seinem Handy beantwortet, während ich zugeschaut und in mich hinein geschmunzelt habe, weil er wie erwartet alles genauso eingeschätzt hat wie ich. Leider zeigte die Auswertung meine Aussagen nicht korrekt, sondern genau anders herum, was wir direkt besprechen und klären konnten, weil wir zusammen wohnen/ bei einander waren in diesem Moment, aber wenn ich mir vorstelle, dass so ein Technik Problem zu Beziehungsproblemen führt, weil ein frisches Paar sich auf die Ergebnisse der App verlässt… Schade!
Ebenso wurden einige Fragen als „negativ“ ausgelegt, wenn das Paar sie gegenteilig beantwortet hat, aber das trifft ja nicht immer zu (z. B. der eine erobert gerne, der andere wird gerne erobert). 
Ansonsten würde es großen Spaß machen und die Quize sind toll, um sich kennenzulernen - wenn die Antworten, die man gegeben hat, korrekt wären und die Auswertungen anders analysiert werden würden.

title: Für 80% Rabatt - 30Fr.
text:
Meine Partnerin und ich haben die App über ein Jahr hinweg genutzt. Während unseres Urlaubs haben wir das Tagesjournal täglich verwendet und die Fragen regelmäßig beantwortet. Dabei ist uns aufgefallen, dass sich viele Fragen stark ähnelten und inhaltlich meist identisch waren, lediglich anders formuliert. Trotz dieser Wiederholungen haben wir die Funktion weiterhin genutzt.

An mehreren Tagen wurden unsere eingegebenen Antworten jedoch nicht gespeichert, was sehr frustrierend war. Zusätzlich mussten wir bereits mehrfach jeweils 1.– CHF bezahlen, um die sogenannten „Flammen“ zu retten.

Nun, da das Abonnement ausläuft, wird mir ein angeblicher Rabatt von 80 % angeboten, sodass ich für ein weiteres Jahr 30.– CHF bezahlen soll. Aus meiner Sicht ist dieses Preis-Leistungs-Verhältnis nicht nachvollziehbar und wirkt eher wie eine Abzocke.

Positiv hervorzuheben ist lediglich die Möglichkeit, Erinnerungen mit Fotos zu speichern sowie bestehende Termine einzutragen. Die übrigen Funktionen, insbesondere die Themen- und Tagesjournal-Fragen, wirkten größtenteils austauschbar und wie automatisch generiert, lediglich sprachlich variiert.

Für den gebotenen Funktionsumfang ist ein Preis von 30.– CHF pro Jahr, selbst mit beworbenem Rabatt, deutlich überhöht. Ein fairer Preis läge aus meiner Sicht eher bei maximal 15.– CHF jährlich.

Ein Jahrespreis von 30.– CHF mit angeblichen 80 % Rabatt ist daher wenig glaubwürdig und wirkt nicht seriös.

title: A Cash Grab Disguised as an App – Rizz is a Complete Letdown
text:
I usually don’t write reviews, but my experience with the Rizz app was frustrating enough that I felt the need to warn others before they waste their time or money. This app is a textbook example of a modern bait-and-switch – promising innovative features, sleek design, and helpful tools, but hiding everything even remotely useful behind an aggressive paywall.

Let me break it down:

1. Absolutely No Free Functionality

The most glaring issue with Rizz is that there is nothing – and I mean nothing – useful you can do on this app without paying. The app markets itself as some kind of revolutionary social AI assistant or “rizz generator” (whatever that means), but the moment you open it, you’re greeted with pop-ups to upgrade or subscribe. You can’t even test the core functionality to see if it’s worth it. No trial, no basic version, no limited access. Just a brick wall with a price tag on it.

If you’re expecting even a basic feature set to be free – like a few messages, sample profiles, or basic prompts – forget about it. The “free” version exists in name only. It’s a glorified advertisement for their premium plan.

2. Shady Monetization Strategy

Rizz isn’t just subscription-based – it pushes you into premium tiers with outrageous pricing. You’ll be asked to cough up a monthly fee that’s comparable to full-featured productivity software like Notion, ChatGPT Plus, or Adobe tools – but for what? A chatbot that spits out generic compliments and recycled flirty one-liners?

There are constant prompts, misleading buttons, and sneaky UI tricks to get you to tap “Subscribe.” Some buttons look like regular features, but tapping them immediately leads to a payment page. It feels predatory, like the developers prioritized squeezing money out of users over offering any genuine value.

3. Misleading Marketing

The app’s description and promotional material make it sound like it will enhance your dating life with AI-powered conversation help, message templates, pickup lines, and smooth responses. But the reality is a watered-down, poorly executed chatbot with painfully limited use unless you pay. Even then, the premium features don’t deliver anything you couldn’t find online for free.

Their “AI” is no more intelligent than a random Instagram caption generator. And no, it doesn’t “learn from your conversations” – that’s just fluff to make the tech sound smarter than it is.

4. Poor User Experience

Aside from the paywall nightmare, the app itself is clunky and slow. Navigating between tabs is laggy, and half the time it takes several seconds just to load a simple menu. Notifications don’t work properly, and there are frequent crashes. The UI is overly flashy but unintuitive, with confusing layouts that seem more interested in looking “modern” than actually being usable.

5. No Value for Money

Even if you do decide to shell out cash, you’ll quickly realize how shallow the content is. There’s a small collection of recycled templates and generic messages that feel like they were scraped from Reddit in 2018. The AI doesn’t adapt, doesn’t learn, and doesn’t impress. If you’re looking for genuine help with conversations or flirting, you’d be better off reading a few free blog articles or watching YouTube videos – at least those have some depth and variety.

6. Support is Useless

If you think contacting support will help, think again. There’s no real customer service – just a chatbot with auto-replies. I reached out about the misleading “free” access and received nothing but canned responses and an unhelpful link to their FAQ. No refunds, no accountability, no dialogue.

⸻

Final Verdict: 1/5 Stars (And that’s generous)

Rizz is a perfect example of everything that’s wrong with mobile apps in 2025. It promises innovation but delivers frustration. It hides basic functionality behind an aggressive paywall. It pretends to be smart but ends up being generic. It offers no trial, no transparency, and no reason to trust it.

Unless you’re interested in paying a premium subscription just to test whether it’s worth anything (spoiler: it’s not), I strongly recommend avoiding this app. There are far better tools out there – many of them free – that actually help with communication, relationships, or self-confidence.

Don’t fall for the hype. Rizz is all marketing and no substance.

I recently gave the Rizz app a try, hoping to find some entertaining and clever pick-up lines to lighten the mood and spark interesting conversations. However, my experience with the app left me utterly unimpressed and cringing at the sheer corniness of the pick-up lines it offered. This app is nothing more than a cornball's paradise, and I cannot recommend it to anyone seeking genuine or witty interactions.

First and foremost, the pick-up lines provided on the Rizz app were embarrassingly cheesy and lacked any semblance of originality. It felt as if the developers had scraped the bottom of the barrel for tired and overused clichés. Instead of offering clever or creative lines that could potentially make someone smile or laugh, I was met with unimaginative and cringe-inducing attempts at humor.

Moreover, the pick-up lines were often ineffective and unrealistic in real-world scenarios. It's one thing to embrace humor and lightheartedness in an attempt to break the ice, but the lines on this app were so far-fetched and forced that they came across as insincere and even creepy. It felt like a desperate attempt to impress rather than a genuine effort to connect with someone.

Another glaring issue with the Rizz app was the lack of variety and customization in the pick-up lines. The app provided a limited pool of lines that quickly became repetitive and predictable. There was no option to personalize or tailor the lines to suit individual preferences or situations. This lack of flexibility made the whole experience feel monotonous and uninspiring.

Furthermore, the user interface and overall design of the app were subpar. It was clunky and unappealing, making navigation a cumbersome task. The app lacked any engaging or interactive elements that could have made the experience more enjoyable. It was clear that the developers focused more on quantity rather than quality, neglecting essential aspects of user experience.

title: Slow loading shortcuts widget, doesn’t truly block app shortcuts
text: This app is a simple widget. The shortcuts look ugly when they load which is contradictory to the aesthetic promised, and they take too long to load compared to just loading them as is. There are hardly any installed shortcuts to most mainstream mail and other apps, so you will be spending too much time creating custom shortcuts if you keep this, and you can make shortcuts on your own for free. There is no point to the app which doesn’t block out other apps. When your device slides to the right, it looks and acts like you never installed the widget. Fair, but I wasn’t expecting that this is just a widget app and not something to block out everything like a mock operating system. An app within an app, you know? I feel bad but this really isn’t worth it. The distractions are going to be there when you slide your finger to the right and the device shows you the apps you have installed anyway with the regular style of the original Home Screen style layout. Would not recommend. I feel so bad writing this review because the intentions seem honest. It’s better to go out and buy yourself a dumb device or, as mentioned, make shortcuts with a black or white background image for free. There is an expensive dumb smartphone out by some Swiss brand called Punk MC02 that does this but works quickly. It’s too pricy for me to spend for minimalism and alleged tech privacy when I can use a computer, but it will do the job better and is the formatting that this app developer uhhh….took lots of “inspiration” from, to phrase it politely. Look it up on the web and the typeface plus more will all be a bit familiar to this. But the difference is, it would probably work as promised. Seeing the app developer here insists to click reduce motion. Uh nope, this doesn’t make your shortcuts widget any faster… it just is SLOW, never anything decent.

title: Fine, Needs (a lot) More
text:
I’ll change my review if the developer fixed any of the problems I talk about here.

This is an extremely simple app that basically acts as a stylish launcher for Apple Shortcuts.

Shortcuts, which comes included with any recent Apple device, is free & amazing (through no effort of the creator of this app.) Dumbify isn’t different from any of the other free apps that provide minimalist Launcher Widgets, and actually offers less customizability in some cases. That’s why it’s so disappointing how *little* this app does. There are two types of Widgets that Dumbify provides: one that can show links to (Shortcuts that open) apps of your choice, and an empty one that acts as a “spacer” for your home screen. There is only ONE size of Launcher Widget offered, which takes up an entire screen of an iPhone. There is ZERO customization beyond this, which is where I’m frustrated. I’d really really like to see more than one size of Launcher widget offered, or the ability to re-size the Launcher Widget on iOS 18 (running the beta in my iPad, Dumbify *does not* include this super simple functionality.)
The lack of Launcher Widget customization beyond font size/weight is super disappointing too - I’d expect a few options for alternative fonts to the default. 

Dumbify is a product to make your home screen look *exactly* how those in the App Store page’s demo pictures show. If you want anything beyond that (and you likely will after a few hours) go somewhere else.

title: Impossible to cancel trial
text:
I signed up for a free trial and wasn’t impressed, so I went to cancel. The subscription did not appear anywhere in my Apple subscriptions, which is where we’ve been trained to manage app payments.

After signing up, I had received an email from a third-party payment processor (Link), so I followed the link in that email to manage or cancel. The subscription did not appear there either. I contacted Link directly and clearly asked to cancel before the trial ended.

Despite this, I was charged for a full year of the app. I am now waiting on a refund while Link says they are “looking into this,” which has been going on for days.

The app itself may or may not be useful, but the billing and cancellation experience is confusing, non-transparent, and frustrating.  iPhone users should be very cautious, as this is not handled through Apple’s normal subscription system.

To make matters worse, even though they fixed the breach, they still don’t have the level of encryption their competitors offer. Imagine having all of your private logs and most personal information in your recovery journey become publicly readable. 

I just wanted a refund from my subscription as it was less than 24 hours from when I got it. I didn’t want to leave any negative review.  At the end of the day this company will take every dollar it can from people. Just look at all the reviews of people who were scammed into thinking they got a lifetime subscription. I get as a company wanting to make a profit, but there’s no need to be sloppy with policy and reckless with data security. Thankfully there are other secure alternatives that genuinely help and care about security. Hope I have prevented at least one person from making the same mistake as I have.

title: Did not work
text: This game is extremely frustrating because it does not properly sync with my TikTok account, which makes it basically unplayable. No matter how many times I try to connect my TikTok or refresh the app, it keeps saying that I need more likes, even though I am very active on TikTok and clearly meet the requirements. I am on TikTok constantly, engaging with content, liking posts, and interacting daily, yet the game still does not recognize any of that activity. Because of this, I am locked out of features and unable to progress at all. The app gives no clear explanation or solution, and there is no helpful support to fix the problem. It feels misleading and poorly designed, especially since the game heavily relies on TikTok integration to function. Until the syncing issue is fixed and the game accurately reflects real TikTok activity, I would not recommend this app to anyone.
